title: Beat the baseline
goal: Score above 0.70 overall on simple factual questions
hint: The agentic pipeline doesn't help on simple, single-fact lookups — it just adds latency. Try the naive pipeline with a dense embedding model first.
concept: Naive RAG (single retrieve + generate) is the right tool for direct factual lookups. Agentic decomposition earns its cost only on multi-hop or ambiguous queries.

title: The exact-match problem
goal: Reach recall@3 above 0.9 on questions containing code snippets
hint: Dense embeddings blur exact tokens like function names and variable identifiers. A sparse or hybrid retriever preserves exact-match signal.
concept: BM25 (sparse, term-frequency based) excels at exact-token queries — code, IDs, error codes — where dense embeddings lose precision. Hybrid RRF combines both strengths.

title: Multi-hop mastery
goal: Score above 0.75 overall on multi-document questions
hint: A single retrieval pass can't gather evidence spread across multiple documents. Try the agentic pipeline with query decomposition.
concept: Agentic decomposition breaks a multi-hop question into sub-questions, retrieves for each independently, then synthesizes — this is what naive single-shot RAG structurally cannot do.

title: Don't hallucinate
hint: A model that always tries to answer will hallucinate when the corpus has no relevant information. Raise the confidence threshold so low-evidence queries fall back to 'insufficient evidence'.
concept: Confidence scoring (composite or NLI-based) lets the pipeline recognize when retrieved evidence doesn't support an answer, and refuse gracefully instead of hallucinating.

title: Speed vs quality
goal: Score above 0.70 overall while keeping average latency under 5000ms
hint: Agentic pipelines and large models are slow. Caching, a smaller/faster model, or skipping reranking on easy queries can recover latency without giving up much quality.
concept: Every quality gain has a latency cost. Production RAG systems tune the whole pipeline against a latency budget, not just accuracy in isolation — this is the core tradeoff of Skill 5's NFR table.
